prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the geometry of a narrow paved path stretching straight ahead, flanked closely on the left and right by dense bushes and tall trees creating a corridor layout, with a bright continuous ground gradient from less than 1 metre at the bottom edge out to dark receding distances over 30 metres away at the centre vanishing point. In frames 1 and 2, a vertical lamppost on the left approaches from roughly 10-12 metres away to about 3-4 metres away just above the left bushes, while the low foliage on the left and right edges passes within 1 to 2 metres (nearly within arm's reach) of the forward-moving camera wearer. Distant figures further down the path (around 15-40 metres ahead in frames 2-5, spaced roughly 10-20 metres apart from each other) are barely visible until frame 5, where a distinct grey silhouette of a cyclist on the centre-left of the path stands out at roughly 12-15 metres ahead. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the 3D tunnel-like enclosure of the overhanging tree canopy, the foreground bush protrusions, and the sharp vertical profile of the lamppost in frame 2 much easier to separate from the cluttered green foliage. However, the map is unreliable for small distant people in frames 2-4 where they blend into the background darkness, and around fine porous tree branches and leaves against the sky where depth edges appear jagged or perforated.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is almost entirely blank black across frames 1 to 4, detecting no objects, vegetation, or distant people until frame 5, where a single pink mask labelled 'person' appears on the path slightly to the left of centre. In conjunction with the RGB context, this detected person is a cyclist roughly 12-15 metres in front of the camera wearer, positioned on the left side of the paved trail and either facing away or inline with the path (too distant to discern gaze, with nothing within the camera wearer's arm's reach). Across the 5 frames, as the camera wearer moves forward along the trail, this person's relative size increases enough by frame 5 to cross the detector's threshold, isolating their silhouette more clearly than the dark shadowed RGB foliage behind them. Nevertheless, the segmentation map is highly unreliable for comprehensive scene understanding here: it completely misses the bicycle directly beneath and overlapping the person in frame 5, fails to segment the same cyclist and another more distant person visible at roughly 15-40 metres in frames 2-4, and provides no masks for static obstacles like the lamppost or flanking bushes.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all 5 frames, containing no yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the strip. Using the RGB context, this complete absence of detections occurs because no hands or body parts of the camera wearer enter the egocentric field of view (nothing is held within arm's reach in frame), and the other people on the path remain too far ahead—ranging from roughly 30-40 metres away in frames 2-3 to about 12-15 metres away in frame 5—for keypoint extraction. Consequently, the pose map alone provides no direct information about scene layout, relative positions, occlusions, body orientation, or whether anyone is looking toward the camera wearer as the wearer advances along the path. It adds nothing beyond the RGB image other than confirming the absence of close-range human figures, and is entirely unreliable for tracking distant pedestrians or cyclists whose small pixel footprint in frames 2-5 prevents skeleton estimation.
